postText:
Today, 26th of July, we commemorate the Internationa Day for the Conservation of Mangroves Ecosystem.   

According to Dr. Jurgenne Primavera,  Philippines' leading scientist and expert on Mangroves, "The Philippines harbour 39 species of true mangroves belonging to the following genera: Acanthus, Camptostemon, Lumnitzera, Excoecaria, Pemphis, Xylocarpus, Aegiceras, Osbornia, Nypa, Aegialitis, Bruguiera, Ceriops, Kandelia, Rhizophora, Scyphiphora, and Sonneratia." 

Its ecosystem services range from food such as fish and shrimp, other species collected from mangroves are crabs and lobsters, bivalve and gastropod molluscs, and other invertebrates. Other services include coastal protection, erosion control, sediment stabilization, flood regulation, nutrient supply and regeneration, waste treatment, and wildlife habitats.  

The decline of mangroves from about 500,000 ha in 1918 to only 120,500 ha in 1994 was caused by overexploitation caused by coastal land conversions to human settlements, agriculture, aquaculture, salt pans, and industry. 

Let us help conserve our 'super' mangrove forests by joining reforestation and conservation efforts and living a Zero Waste lifestyle!  Please share!
